scenes.title: Where and when
narration: Jumpstyle emerged in Belgium around 1997–1998, drawing roots from Chicago hard house and European hard dance.
It gained significant commercial traction between 2006 and 2008, fueled by artists like Patrick Jumpen and Scooter, before evolving into a digital-first community in the 2010s and 2020s.

scenes.title: When it is danced
narration: Jumpstyle is practiced as a social dance in clubs, at organized 'jumpmeetings' in public spaces, and through online video competitions.
It is described as a 'solitaire and apolitique' dance that evolves based on regional influences.
Today it is a living tradition.

scenes.title: Watch it
narration: Dancers perform 'jumpen' by executing kicks and jumps in time with the 909 kick drum.
The upper body remains relatively stiff, with expressive movement concentrated in the legs.
Dancers may perform solo, in pairs (duojump), or in large groups, often synchronizing footwork and rotations.
Watch for Duo-kick, Spins.

scenes.title: Listen
narration: The music is characterized by a 140–160 BPM tempo and a four-on-the-floor 909 kick drum.
Later developments incorporated hardstyle influences, including pitched basslines, multiband distortion, and synthesizers utilizing square waveforms.
Listen for the synthesizers with square waveforms, drum machine (909), distorted basslines.
The pulse is 4/4 at about 150 beats a minute.
A high-tempo electronic sound defined by a heavy, repetitive 909 kick drum and melodic, distorted synthesizer leads.

scenes.title: The people
narration: Key figures include Da Boy Tommy, Patrick Jumpen, the duo Jeckyll & Hyde, and the Lithuanian rapper Yabujin, who pioneered the Yabujin-core revival.

Variants include oldschool (early basic steps), hardjump (six-touch base), sidejump (rotational focus), hardfreestyle (hybrid of hardjump and sidejump), ownstyle (highly personalized, modern standard), and tekstyle (industrial jump).
Jumpstyle evolved from tech-trance, hardstyle, gabber, and mákina, and has influenced modern internet-based genres like Yabujincore.
